evidence: DIMENSION WEIGHTS: task/tests/scoring.toml is byte-identical to the frozen template scoring.toml (diff clean): [gates] render=0.0 constraints=0.0; [weights] functional=0.6 polish=0.2 visual=0.2; [floors] functional=0.05. task/tests/tools/score.py is identical to the template (diff clean); score.py:46-48 computes weighted=sum(w*score)/sum(w) and sets reward=0.0 unless gates_passed and functional>0.05. This matches SKILL.md Delivery profile and Internal Quality Checks E45 ('Functionality has 60 percent'). Functional therefore outweighs structure/style 0.6 vs 0.4, and no dimension weight lives in any judge.toml [judge] block. MAX NON-FUNCTIONAL CONTRIBUTION (sanity check per quality-checks.md #44): polish+visual cap at 0.4. Polish is not farmable by a shell: every polish row is a behavioural check (draft/focus/scroll preservation under live updates, earlier-page anchoring, failed-send retry, session-expiry resume), and hro_pol_live_board / hro_pol_live_thread explicitly score 0 'If no update arrives within 15 seconds'. Visual (0.2) is the only dimension a weakly functional app could earn, and only after both gates (real shared job+candidate creation with independent-context readback) and functional>0.05 (>2.925 of 58.5 functional weight units). Worst plausible farming case: gate-passing app with ~3 functional units (e.g. job_open 0.5 + add_candidate 0.5 + add_email_rules 1 + arrive_bottom 1) plus perfect visuals = 0.6*0.051+0.2 ~= 0.23, versus a fully working plain-looking app at >= 0.6+0.2*(polish)+0.2*~0.4 ~= 0.68+. Function dominates; that floor/cap design is template policy, not a task choice. PER-CRITERION WEIGHTS (computed by tomllib from the frozen judge.toml files): functional 43 binary criteria, total 58.5; polish 5 binary, total 12.0; visual 5 likert points=5, equal 1.2 each (total 6.0). Highest functional weights (2.5 each, 4.3% of functional) are hro_stale_refused, hro_live_board, hro_candidate_private - exactly the brief's headline promises ('the hard part is that nobody's work gets trampled', 'within fifteen seconds without a reload', 'They must never see our internal notes, why someone was rejected, or anyone else'). 2.0 tier: hro_refused_put_back, hro_bulk_all_or_none, hro_undo_restores, hro_undo_conflict, hro_thread_earlier, hro_unread_counts, hro_unread_scrolled_up, hro_drafts - each is an explicit, hard-to-implement promise in instruction.md paragraphs 2-4 and hireops_rules.md sections 3 and 6. Lowest tier (0.5): hro_job_open, hro_add_candidate, hro_reject_hired, hro_undo_full, hro_activity_refusals, hro_candidate_linked - simple CRUD/validation or narrow edge refusals whose positive path is already required by hro_gate_shared (job + candidate creation with independent readback) or by sibling rows; low weight is honest for low marginal proof. Product-area balance: board/pipeline rows (job_open..undo_once, activity, notes, live_board) ~= 38-39 units (~0.40 of reward) and conversation/candidate rows ~= 19-21 units (~0.20) plus conversation-centric polish (earlier_place, live_thread, failed_send, session_resume = 9.5/12 of polish ~= 0.16); the brief says 'Two things happen in it', so the two halves carry comparable mass. Polish internal weights favour the brief's explicit preservation promises (live_board 3, live_thread 3, session_resume 2.5) over the narrower failed_send 1.5. Visual equal weights are reasonable for five parallel craft facets and the dimension sum is fixed by scoring.toml regardless. No style-only criterion sits in functional or polish; no structural criterion (file layout, routes, framework) is weighted anywhere. ADVERSARIAL PROBES: (1) Broken app that could score high: a fully featured app with no live push loses functional live_board/msg_exchange/unread_counts/unread_scrolled_up/seen (9.5/58.5*0.6 ~= 0.097) plus polish live rows (6/12*0.2 = 0.10) ~= 0.2 total, proportionate to 'Other people's moves should show up on my board within fifteen seconds' being a headline requirement; a board-only app without conversations loses ~0.36; a pretty shell fails the gates (0.0). None scores near a conforming app. (2) Conforming alternative that could lose disproportionately: correlated preconditions (polish live rows requiring a live update) only bite when the live feature is absent, which is a real defect; a conforming app that refuses a bad move before optimistic display still passes hro_refused_put_back by its own text. I found no weight arrangement that penalises a conforming design choice. Observations noted but not defects: hro_activity (1.0) bundles seven event kinds plus filter for modest weight, and hro_job_open (0.5) bundles five validation refusals - both under-weight rather than over-weight non-functional content, so they cannot make style outrank function. Realised reward ordering/discrimination is unmeasured (raw-evidence-index.json scope: 'reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent'); that measurement is owned by rows 40/42 and the runtime records, and is not required to judge the static weight assignment for this row.
